location.en: Port Aurora old town, free walking tour
location.zh: 極光港舊城區，免費徒步導覽

goal.en: Ask the guide good questions, interrupt politely and end the tour the right way.
goal.zh: 向導遊提出好問題、禮貌地打斷發問，並用正確的方式結束導覽。

background: old harbor town street with a white stone lighthouse at the end, cobblestone path, colorful wooden houses, iron lamp posts, fishing boats in the water, bright morning

intro.en: The next morning, you join a free walking tour of Port Aurora's old town. The guide holds a yellow umbrella high in the air.
intro.zh: 隔天早上，你們參加極光港舊城區的免費徒步導覽。導遊把一把黃色雨傘高高舉起。

intro.en: Follow the yellow umbrella, everyone! First stop: the lighthouse.
intro.zh: 各位跟著黃色雨傘走！第一站：燈塔。

lines.en: This is the Aurora Lighthouse, the oldest building in the city.
lines.zh: 這是極光燈塔，全市最古老的建築。

lines.en: Whoa. Kai, ask him how old it is!
lines.zh: 哇。凱，問他這座燈塔多老了！

choices.en: How old is the lighthouse, exactly?
choices.zh: 這座燈塔確切是多老呢？
choices.tip: How old is + 名詞？可以問建築或物品的年代，跟問人的年紀同一個句型。

choices.en: This lighthouse has how many years?

lines.en: How many years... of what? Of me working here? Eleven!
lines.zh: 幾年……什麼的幾年？我在這裡工作幾年嗎？十一年！

story.en: Felix proudly tells you about his eleven years as a guide. You learn a lot about Felix and nothing about the lighthouse.
story.zh: 菲力克斯驕傲地分享他當導遊的十一年。你對菲力克斯了解很多，對燈塔一無所知。

fail.why: 「有幾年了」直譯成 has how many years，英文沒有這種說法，疑問詞也要放句首。問年代要說 How old is the lighthouse?

choices.en: Cool. And how old are you, Felix?

lines.en: Me? Uh... older than I look. Let's stick to the lighthouse!
lines.zh: 我？呃……比看起來老一點。我們還是聊燈塔吧！

story.en: The whole tour group turns to look at you. Felix walks a little faster for the rest of the morning.
story.zh: 整團的人都轉頭看你。接下來一整個早上，菲力克斯都走得有點快。

fail.why: 在英語文化裡，直接問不熟的大人幾歲很失禮。想知道燈塔的年代，問 How old is the lighthouse? 就好。

lines.en: It was built in 1852. Sailors say a ghost still keeps the light on at night.
lines.zh: 它建於 1852 年。水手們說，晚上還有個鬼魂在顧著燈火。

lines.en: A ghost? Kai, I need to hear this!
lines.zh: 鬼魂？凱，我一定要聽這個！

choices.en: Could you tell us more about the ghost?
choices.zh: 可以多跟我們說一些鬼魂的事嗎？
choices.tip: Could you tell us more about...? 是請對方多說一點的禮貌句型。

choices.en: Can you telling us more the ghost story?
choices.zh: 你可以多說一點鬼故事嗎？

lines.en: Telling you... the ghost? Sorry, I lost you there.
lines.zh: 告訴你……鬼魂？抱歉，我沒聽懂。

story.en: Felix decides it wasn't important and moves on to the next stop. Leo never gets his ghost story.
story.zh: 菲力克斯覺得應該不重要，就往下一站走了。里歐最終沒聽到他的鬼故事。

fail.why: can 後面要接原形動詞 tell，不能接 telling；tell us more 後面也要加 about。可以說 Could you tell us more about the ghost?

choices.en: Tell us more about the ghost. Go on, now.
choices.zh: 多講一點鬼魂的事。快講啊。

lines.en: Oh. Uh, sure... if you insist.
lines.zh: 喔。呃，好吧……既然你這麼堅持。

story.en: Felix tells the story in a flat voice, like he's reading a phone bill. It is the least scary ghost story ever.
story.zh: 菲力克斯用平板的語氣講完，像在念電話帳單。這是史上最不恐怖的鬼故事。

fail.why: 祈使句加上 Go on, now 像在命令對方。請人多說一點，用 Could you tell us more about...? 聽起來有禮貌又有興趣。

lines.en: At the old market, Felix talks faster and faster. You miss something important.
lines.zh: 到了舊市場，菲力克斯越講越快。你漏聽了重要的一段。

lines.en: ...so after the fire, the whole market moved to the pier, and then in 1925...
lines.zh: ……所以大火之後，整個市場搬到碼頭，然後在 1925 年……

choices.en: Sorry to interrupt, but what fire was that?
choices.zh: 抱歉打斷一下，那是什麼大火？
choices.tip: Sorry to interrupt, but... 是打斷別人發問時最禮貌的開場。

choices.en: Stop, stop! You talk too fast. Again!
choices.zh: 停、停！你講太快了。再講一次！

lines.en: Oh. Okay... from the very beginning, then?

story.en: Felix starts over from the year 1700, very slowly. The tour runs an hour late, and the group is not happy.
story.zh: 菲力克斯從西元 1700 年開始，非常緩慢地重講一遍。導覽延遲了一小時，整團的人都不太開心。

fail.why: 連喊 Stop 再用命令句，對導遊很不禮貌。想打斷發問，說 Sorry to interrupt, but what fire was that? 就好。

choices.en: Excuse me, you can say again the fire part?
choices.zh: 不好意思，你可以再說一次大火那段嗎？

lines.en: Say again... which part? The market part? Sure!
lines.zh: 再說一次……哪一段？市場那段嗎？沒問題！

story.en: Felix happily repeats everything about the market. You still have no idea what burned down.
story.zh: 菲力克斯開心地把市場的部分重講一遍。你還是不知道到底燒掉了什麼。

fail.why: 疑問句要把 can 放句首，say again 後面也不能直接接名詞。可以說 Could you say that again? 或 Sorry to interrupt, but what fire was that?

lines.en: And that's the end of the tour! It's pay-what-you-like, so tips are always welcome.
lines.zh: 導覽到這裡結束！採自由付費，所以很歡迎大家給小費。

choices.en: Thanks, Felix! This is from the three of us.
choices.zh: 謝謝你，菲力克斯！這是我們三個的心意。
choices.tip: 免費導覽結束時給導遊小費是慣例，遞錢時說 This is from us. 很自然。

choices.en: Great, free tour! Thanks, see you, Felix!
choices.zh: 太好了，免費導覽！謝啦，掰掰，菲力克斯！

lines.en: Uh... bye. Tips are welcome, though.
lines.zh: 呃……掰。不過還是歡迎給小費喔。

story.en: Everyone else drops a few dollars into Felix's hat. Your goodbye sounds much quieter than theirs.
story.zh: 其他人都在菲力克斯的帽子裡放了幾塊錢。你的道別聽起來比大家小聲多了。

fail.why: free walking tour 的導遊主要靠小費維生，聽完通常會給 5 到 20 元。說 Thanks! This is from us. 再把小費交給他。

choices.en: Tips? Sure! My tip is: try bubble tea in Taiwan.
choices.zh: 建議？好啊！我的建議是：去台灣喝珍奶。

lines.en: Ha, good tip... but I meant the money kind.
lines.zh: 哈，好建議……不過我說的是錢的那種。

story.en: The whole group laughs, and so do you. Then Mia quietly pays the tip for all three of you.
story.zh: 整團都笑了，你也跟著笑。然後米亞默默幫你們三個付了小費。

fail.why: tip 有「小費」和「小建議」兩個意思，導覽結束時說 tips are welcome 指的是小費。可以說 Thanks! This is from us.，再把錢交給導遊。

lines.en: Thank you, you three! Hungry? The Salty Anchor by the pier has the best fish in town.
lines.zh: 謝謝你們三位！肚子餓了嗎？碼頭邊的鹹錨餐廳有全城最好吃的魚。

lines.en: Best fish in town? Write that down, Kai!
lines.zh: 全城最好吃的魚？凱，快記下來！

story.en: You heard the ghost story, learned about the great fire and got a local tip, the useful kind. Port Aurora feels a little less like a stranger now.
story.zh: 你聽到了鬼故事，搞懂了那場大火，還拿到在地人推薦（有用的那種 tip）。極光港感覺不再那麼陌生了。

notes.en: Could you tell us more about...?
notes.zh: 可以多跟我們說一些……嗎？
notes.explain: 請導遊或任何人多說一點時用的禮貌句型。Could you 後面接原形動詞，about 後面接主題。

example.en: Could you tell us more about the old market?
example.zh: 可以多跟我們說一些舊市場的事嗎？

notes.explain: How old is + 名詞 可以問建築或物品的年代。回答時說 It was built in 1852. 或 It's over 170 years old.。

example.en: How old is this bridge? It was built in 1910.
example.zh: 這座橋多老了？它建於 1910 年。

notes.explain: 打斷別人說話時的禮貌開場。英語文化很習慣聽眾發問，聽不懂就直接問，不用假裝聽懂。

example.en: Sorry to interrupt, but could you say that again?
example.zh: 抱歉打斷一下，可以再說一次嗎？

notes.en: Tipping on a free walking tour
notes.explain: free walking tour 或 pay-what-you-like 的導遊主要靠小費維生，結束時一人給 5 到 20 元是常見做法。另外，直接問不熟的大人幾歲也很失禮。

example.en: Thanks for the great tour! This is for you.
example.zh: 謝謝你精彩的導覽！這是給你的。

notes.explain: tip 有兩個意思：給服務人員的小費，以及實用的小建議。Tips are welcome 出現在導覽或餐廳結尾時，幾乎都是指小費。

example.en: Here's a tip: book the restaurant early. And don't forget to leave a tip!
example.zh: 給你個建議：餐廳要早點訂。還有別忘了給小費！
